stages.title: Validate the customer problem
stages.summary: Confirm the proposal bottleneck before choosing software.

tasks.title: Choose a region and contractor segment
tasks.description: Name the geography and contractor type you will investigate first.

tasks.title: Interview five operators
tasks.description: Use the discovery script and record evidence without inventing demand.

tasks.title: Record the current quotation and follow-up process
tasks.description: Map the hand-offs, delays, owners, and tools used today.

stages.title: Explore and adapt the demonstration
stages.summary: Map required fields and calculations to an approved scope.

tasks.title: List materials and labour inputs
tasks.description: Capture only the inputs needed for an initial quotation workflow.

tasks.title: Define quotation states
tasks.description: Agree the states, owners, and next actions used in the pipeline.

tasks.title: Remove features the customer does not need
tasks.description: Keep the pilot bounded by documenting excluded features explicitly.

stages.title: Define the offer and project scope
stages.summary: Bound the setup, migration, training, and support commitments.

tasks.title: Write a scope sheet
tasks.description: List the configuration, migration, training, and handover work included.

tasks.title: Define ownership and support limits
tasks.description: Record responsibilities, revision limits, hosting, and ongoing support boundaries.

stages.title: Research suitable potential customers
stages.summary: Build a small, relevant outreach list.

tasks.title: Identify 20 local contractors
tasks.description: Create a focused list using public business information.

tasks.title: Prioritise teams with bespoke quotations
tasks.description: Rank prospects whose work appears to require complex proposal follow-up.

stages.title: Demonstrate the solution and agree a pilot
stages.summary: Use fictional or authorised sample data in a focused walkthrough.

tasks.title: Prepare a 15-minute demo
tasks.description: Show the agreed workflow using fictional or authorised sample records.

tasks.title: Agree success and exit criteria
tasks.description: Document what the pilot will test and how either party can stop it.

stages.title: Test, launch, and support
stages.summary: Verify access, backups, and communication before handover.

tasks.title: Run permission tests
tasks.description: Verify each role can access only the records and actions it needs.

tasks.title: Document recovery and ownership
tasks.description: Record backup, recovery, credential, and support responsibilities.

stages.title: Understand the clinic opportunity
stages.summary: Choose one administrative workflow to investigate without assuming demand.

tasks.title: Choose one administrative workflow
tasks.description: Name the enquiry, appointment, follow-up, payment, task, or reporting workflow you will investigate first.

tasks.title: Write the operations-software boundary
tasks.description: Record that the offer is not an EHR, EMR, clinical decision system, or compliance-certified product.

stages.title: Explore the CRM
stages.summary: Review only the demo capabilities that have been supplied and verified.

tasks.title: Confirm the demo evidence available
tasks.description: Record the supplied URL, synthetic-data notice, observed navigation, and any unverified areas.

tasks.title: Prepare a bounded walkthrough
tasks.description: Plan a short walkthrough using only verified features and synthetic data.

stages.title: Choose a clinic segment
stages.summary: Keep the first discovery effort focused on one clinic category and location.

tasks.title: Choose one clinic category
tasks.description: Select one discovery target such as dental, physiotherapy, aesthetic, wellness, or another specialty clinic.

tasks.title: Choose one location
tasks.description: Define a practical city or region for the initial research.

stages.title: Research potential customers
stages.summary: Build a small list from published business information without inventing buyers.

tasks.title: Create a verified research list
tasks.description: Record clinic name, website, category, location, published business contact route, source, and last checked date.

tasks.title: Verify contact routes
tasks.description: Check each business and contact route manually before respectful one-to-one outreach.

stages.title: Define your service package
stages.summary: Turn the proposed work into a bounded scope with clear responsibilities.

tasks.title: Write inclusions and exclusions
tasks.description: List configuration, customisation, training, handover, integrations, and work that is explicitly excluded.

tasks.title: Model delivery cost
tasks.description: Use your own direct-cost, time, and fee assumptions without treating the result as a market-price recommendation.

stages.title: Prepare the CRM demo
stages.summary: Use fictional records and match the walkthrough to the researched workflow.

tasks.title: Prepare fictional demonstration data
tasks.description: Confirm the walkthrough contains no real clinic or patient information.

tasks.title: Map the demo to the workflow
tasks.description: Select only verified features that relate to the clinic's administrative process.

stages.title: Speak with clinics
stages.summary: Learn how the current administrative process works before proposing software.

tasks.title: Run discovery conversations
tasks.description: Ask about current processes, roles, exceptions, permissions, systems of record, and ownership without collecting patient details.

tasks.title: Record evidence and mismatches
tasks.description: Document what the example does not match and which assumptions remain unverified.

stages.title: Scope a customer implementation
stages.summary: Agree workflow, data, infrastructure, acceptance, and support boundaries.

tasks.title: Agree data responsibilities
tasks.description: Document preparation, authorisation, import, validation, retention, backup, and recovery ownership.

tasks.title: Define acceptance checks
tasks.description: Write testable outcomes, dependencies, exclusions, and the process for changes.

stages.title: Customise and test
stages.summary: Configure the agreed scope and verify it with synthetic or authorised test data.

tasks.title: Configure the agreed workflow
tasks.description: Apply only the approved branding, statuses, fields, roles, permissions, and reports.

tasks.title: Test important and failure flows
tasks.description: Verify permissions, appointments, follow-ups, applicable billing logic, errors, edge cases, backups, and recovery.

stages.title: Deploy and hand over
stages.summary: Transfer a reviewed system with clear ownership, training, limitations, and support.

tasks.title: Confirm production ownership
tasks.description: Record who owns the domain, hosting, backend, credentials, costs, backups, and recovery process.

tasks.title: Complete staff handover
tasks.description: Brief staff, transfer credentials securely, document unresolved limitations, and agree future support.

stages.title: Map the current quotation workflow
stages.summary: Record systems, owners, states, and exceptions.

tasks.title: Identify the source of truth
tasks.description: Name the authorised system that owns quotation status.

tasks.title: Document how replies are recorded
tasks.description: Map how customer replies stop or change follow-up work.

stages.title: Choose reminder intervals
stages.summary: Agree cadence, business-day rules, and exclusions.

tasks.title: Define offsets
tasks.description: Agree when internal follow-up should become due.

tasks.title: List holidays and excluded states
tasks.description: Prevent reminders on unsuitable days or completed records.

stages.title: Configure logic and destinations
stages.summary: Use the customer’s authorised tools and scoped access.

tasks.title: Map fields
tasks.description: Map stable quotation IDs, dates, owners, and statuses between systems.

tasks.title: Configure task and notification destinations
tasks.description: Send internal work only to the agreed responsible people.

stages.title: Test normal and failure scenarios
stages.summary: Prove duplicate prevention and visible failures in a sandbox.

tasks.title: Run the same check twice
tasks.description: Confirm a retry does not create a duplicate internal task.

tasks.title: Test missing data
tasks.description: Confirm incomplete records fail visibly and safely.

tasks.title: Test an expired connection
tasks.description: Confirm an expired authorisation creates an actionable failure.

stages.title: Run a one-person pilot
stages.summary: Limit the first live trial to one responsible team member.

tasks.title: Agree a five-day trial
tasks.description: Keep the first live window short and owned by one person.

tasks.title: Review the audit log daily
tasks.description: Check executions, skips, duplicates, and failures every day.

stages.title: Document ownership and maintenance
stages.summary: Make credentials, alerts, and support boundaries explicit.

tasks.title: Write the handover matrix
tasks.description: Record who owns credentials, alerts, data, and support.

tasks.title: Schedule a maintenance review
tasks.description: Choose when schemas, permissions, and connections will be reviewed.

stages.title: Confirm the customer and operating problem
stages.summary: Record the real finance workflow, responsible people, authoritative systems, and professional-review boundary.

tasks.title: Map the current finance workflow
tasks.description: Document source records, review, approval, posting, reconciliation, reporting, and period-close ownership.

tasks.title: Confirm advice and evidence boundaries
tasks.description: Record the qualified adviser, jurisdiction, currencies, tax/VAT expectations, and claims the implementation must not make.

stages.title: Prepare a relevant synthetic demonstration
stages.summary: Use verified demo evidence and fictional records without presenting localhost or untested actions as public proof.

tasks.title: Choose the relevant demo areas
tasks.description: Select only the dashboard, trading-party, sales, purchase, banking, journal, or reporting areas tied to discovery.

tasks.title: State the demo boundary
tasks.description: Record that data is synthetic, browser-local, resettable, and not production or AI evidence.

stages.title: Define the included software scope
stages.summary: Separate verified source evidence from customer configuration, integrations, and production work.

tasks.title: Select included modules
tasks.description: List included, excluded, optional, and later modules based on the customer's workflow.

tasks.title: Record unverified dependencies
tasks.description: List product-mode Auth/RLS, posting, storage, integrations, reports, backups, recovery, and other acceptance work.

stages.title: Prepare the private implementation environment
stages.summary: Use an authorised source copy, locked dependencies, isolated services, synthetic data, and secret-safe configuration.

tasks.title: Confirm private source authority
tasks.description: Record the approved source revision and keep it outside public assets and member downloads.

tasks.title: Prepare isolated customer services
tasks.description: Define customer-owned development, database, Auth, hosting, email, monitoring, and recovery accounts without production data.

stages.title: Configure finance workflows and controls
stages.summary: Agree records, statuses, roles, approvals, reversals, reconciliation, reports, and audit evidence.

tasks.title: Define roles and controls
tasks.description: Record who may create, review, approve, post, reconcile, reverse, export, and administer each record type.

tasks.title: Approve business configuration
tasks.description: Confirm entities, fiscal periods, accounts, currencies, documents, numbering, payment terms, and tax/VAT review.

stages.title: Decide whether optional AI is in scope
stages.summary: Keep AI disabled unless the customer approves purpose, provider, data, review, cost, tests, and a safe off switch.

tasks.title: Record the AI decision
tasks.description: Mark AI out of scope or approve one narrow assistive task, provider owner, model, region, budget, and data boundary.

tasks.title: Define human review and failure controls
tasks.description: Prevent automatic posting or payment and test unsafe input, incorrect output, outage, rate limit, cost, and disablement.

stages.title: Research suitable businesses
stages.summary: Build a small verified list without fabricating contacts, buying intent, or market demand.

tasks.title: Build a sourced research list
tasks.description: Record business name, website, category, location, published contact route, source, and last-checked date.

tasks.title: Verify relevance and contact route
tasks.description: Check each business manually and write one evidence-based reason the workflow may be relevant before outreach.

stages.title: Run discovery conversations
stages.summary: Use editable templates to learn the workflow without unsupported claims or unverified promises.

tasks.title: Run one workflow-first discovery call
tasks.description: Ask about records, controls, systems, friction, data, advisers, ownership, and acceptance needs before demonstrating.

tasks.title: Confirm discovery notes
tasks.description: Send a factual recap for correction and keep assumptions visibly separate from customer-confirmed requirements.

stages.title: Model delivery costs and fees
stages.summary: Estimate recurring costs, delivery hours, internal cost, customer fees, and projected gross margin from explicit assumptions.

tasks.title: Record cost and hour assumptions
tasks.description: Enter hosting, database, optional AI, monitoring, discovery, configuration, migration, testing, training, and handover assumptions.

tasks.title: Review the projected margin
tasks.description: Check exclusions, contingency, recurring period, taxes, customer terms, and whether the result is commercially acceptable.

stages.title: Agree a bounded customer package
stages.summary: Choose setup, customisation, migration, training, support, maintenance, and later-module scope without fixed assumptions.

tasks.title: Write inclusions and exclusions
tasks.description: Define modules, workflows, integrations, data, training, professional review, AI, support, and work that is explicitly excluded.

tasks.title: Define acceptance evidence
tasks.description: Agree test cases, responsible reviewers, reconciliations, report checks, data sign-off, and the decision to accept or reject delivery.

stages.title: Configure, migrate, and test safely
stages.summary: Implement the accepted scope with synthetic-first testing, least privilege, reconciled data, backups, and rollback.

tasks.title: Configure and test the agreed scope
tasks.description: Verify roles, records, approvals, posting, reconciliation, reports, errors, duplicates, integrations, and audit evidence.

tasks.title: Rehearse and reconcile authorised migration
tasks.description: Map, trial, validate, reconcile, document rejected rows, and obtain customer sign-off before production import.

stages.title: Deploy, train, and hand over
stages.summary: Transfer accepted software, customer-owned accounts, recovery, training, limitations, and support responsibilities.

tasks.title: Verify deployment and recovery
tasks.description: Record the release, environment, monitoring, backup, restore, rollback, incident contacts, and customer recovery access.

tasks.title: Complete training and handover
tasks.description: Train with fictional records and transfer ownership, known limitations, adviser boundaries, maintenance, support, and offboarding.

stages.title: Choose one service and area
stages.summary: Keep the initial research narrow enough to validate.

tasks.title: Define the service category
tasks.description: Choose one specific service with a clear buyer need.

tasks.title: Choose a postcode cluster
tasks.description: Bound the initial demand and provider research geographically.

stages.title: Interview recent buyers
stages.summary: Understand how people search, compare, and decide.

tasks.title: Ask about urgency
tasks.description: Record when and why a buyer needed a provider quickly.

tasks.title: Record trust and qualification questions
tasks.description: Capture the evidence buyers use to compare providers.

stages.title: Discover provider partners
stages.summary: Confirm capacity, coverage, and response expectations.

tasks.title: Interview five providers
tasks.description: Confirm coverage, availability, fit, and response expectations.

tasks.title: Agree a manual pilot handoff
tasks.description: Define who receives, qualifies, and follows up each enquiry.

stages.title: Prototype the enquiry journey
stages.summary: Use fictional submissions and clear consent language.

tasks.title: Draft the landing page
tasks.description: Explain the service, area, handoff, and limitations clearly.

tasks.title: Prototype qualification fields
tasks.description: Collect only the information needed for the agreed handoff.

stages.title: Run a bounded pilot
stages.summary: Track response quality without promising lead volume.

tasks.title: Route enquiries manually
tasks.description: Use the documented consent and partner handoff process.

tasks.title: Review response times and fit
tasks.description: Record whether enquiries were suitable and handled promptly.

stages.title: Understand the product opportunity
stages.summary: Choose the user problem and the responsible scope before changing the software.

tasks.title: Choose one initial user segment
tasks.description: Name the people whose debt-tracking workflow you will investigate first.

tasks.title: Write the financial-information boundary
tasks.description: State that the product organises user-entered information and scenarios; it does not provide regulated financial advice.

stages.title: Explore the verified demo
stages.summary: Inspect the synthetic workflow and separate observed behaviour from untested production claims.

tasks.title: Complete the demo walkthrough
tasks.description: Review overview, debts, transactions, accounts, debt strategy, Telegram, and AI status using synthetic data.

tasks.title: Record evidence and limitations
tasks.description: Write down which behaviours were verified locally and which integrations remain disabled or untested.

stages.title: Define the product scope
stages.summary: Select the smallest useful feature set and its safety rules.

tasks.title: Choose the core features
tasks.description: Select the debt, transaction, account, budget, goal, and payoff tools needed for the first release.

tasks.title: Document financial data rules
tasks.description: Define user ownership, validation, deletion, logging, export, and recovery requirements.

stages.title: Review source governance
stages.summary: Confirm technical readiness and redistribution authority as separate gates.

tasks.title: Review the inspected source matrix
tasks.description: Check the recorded stack, verification evidence, integration boundaries, and unresolved production work.

tasks.title: Obtain redistribution approval
tasks.description: Record explicit ownership or licensing approval before packaging or distributing source code.

stages.title: Plan the rebrand
stages.summary: Replace identity and legal copy without changing financial calculations accidentally.

tasks.title: Inventory brand surfaces
tasks.description: List application metadata, logos, icons, landing copy, manifest, legal pages, support routes, and screenshots.

tasks.title: Define rebrand acceptance checks
tasks.description: Check light and dark assets, mobile icons, metadata, accessibility text, legal ownership, and responsive screens.

stages.title: Configure Telegram safely
stages.summary: Plan an isolated bot, authenticated linking, confirmation, limits, and observable failures.

tasks.title: Review the Telegram architecture
tasks.description: Trace linking, secret validation, draft expiry, confirmation, idempotency, ownership checks, and rate limits.

tasks.title: Prepare isolated bot configuration
tasks.description: Use a separate bot, environment-managed secrets, a dedicated webhook, and synthetic acceptance data.

stages.title: Decide whether to enable AI
stages.summary: Treat AI as an optional, costed interpretation layer—not the financial calculation engine.

tasks.title: Approve the AI data boundary
tasks.description: Review the user-scoped context, redaction, retention, deletion, timeout, and abuse controls before enabling a provider.

tasks.title: Set provider and cost limits
tasks.description: Choose a model, monthly allowance, timeout, disable switch, monitoring owner, and fallback behaviour.

stages.title: Model the business
stages.summary: Compare revenue structures using explicit assumptions rather than earnings promises.

tasks.title: Choose a model to test
tasks.description: Compare free, premium subscription, advertising, and partnership options against user trust and operating cost.

tasks.title: Build a scenario from your assumptions
tasks.description: Record active users, conversion, price, ad RPM, usage, technical costs, and calculated gross margin.

stages.title: Plan subscriptions
stages.summary: Design billing, entitlement, cancellation, tax, and support boundaries before connecting payments.

tasks.title: Define free and premium boundaries
tasks.description: Write clear feature, quota, data, cancellation, and support rules for each proposed tier.

tasks.title: Map billing and entitlement events
tasks.description: Document checkout, webhook verification, idempotency, subscription states, refunds, and server-side access checks.

stages.title: Evaluate advertising
stages.summary: Decide whether ads fit a sensitive financial product before adding any SDK or placement.

tasks.title: Write the advertising policy
tasks.description: Define prohibited categories, sensitive-data boundaries, consent, frequency, placement, and age or geography constraints.

tasks.title: Design a reversible ad experiment
tasks.description: Specify a small placement, success and trust metrics, kill switch, and review owner without connecting a live network.

stages.title: Prepare the launch
stages.summary: Complete privacy, security, reliability, support, and store-readiness checks.

tasks.title: Complete the launch evidence checklist
tasks.description: Verify authentication, RLS, backups, recovery, deletion, analytics consent, legal pages, accessibility, and responsive behaviour.

tasks.title: Assign launch ownership
tasks.description: Name owners for incidents, support, costs, provider dashboards, credentials, rollbacks, and status communication.

stages.title: Plan responsible growth
stages.summary: Choose education-led acquisition loops that preserve trust.

tasks.title: Choose one growth channel
tasks.description: Select a bounded SEO, free-tool, content, social, community, or referral experiment.

tasks.title: Define a learning metric
tasks.description: Measure activation, useful recurring behaviour, retention, referral quality, and support burden—not vanity traffic alone.

stages.title: Operate and improve
stages.summary: Run the product with clear metrics, review rhythms, and user-safety controls.

tasks.title: Create the operating dashboard
tasks.description: Track activation, debt-entry completion, payoff-plan use, retention, error rate, support volume, cost, and deletion requests.

tasks.title: Schedule the review rhythm
tasks.description: Assign weekly product, monthly cost and privacy, and quarterly security and recovery reviews.

stages.title: Understand the opportunity
stages.summary: Define the job-seeker task and the evidence boundary.

tasks.title: Choose one job-search need
tasks.description: Write the specific resume or application task the product should help one audience complete.

tasks.title: Set the claims boundary
tasks.description: Remove guarantees about interviews, jobs, ATS acceptance, traffic, conversion, or revenue.

stages.title: Explore Resumi
stages.summary: Walk through the live product with fictional information.

tasks.title: Complete the live walkthrough
tasks.description: Use fictional information to inspect editing, scoring, templates, preview, PDF options and cover letters.

tasks.title: Record evidence and limitations
tasks.description: Separate observed live behaviour from source-only, disabled and future features.

stages.title: Choose an audience
stages.summary: Select one user group and application context.

tasks.title: Define the initial segment
tasks.description: Choose a narrow audience such as fresh graduates, career changers, or UAE job seekers.

tasks.title: Map the application task
tasks.description: Describe what the user brings, what they need to finish, and what a useful outcome looks like.

stages.title: Choose a business model
stages.summary: Model one approach from conservative assumptions.

tasks.title: Choose a model to test
tasks.description: Select free plus premium, freemium plus AI, one-time, partnerships, advertising, or a bounded hybrid.

tasks.title: Record assumptions and costs
tasks.description: Enter your own traffic, conversion, pricing and operating assumptions without treating the result as a forecast.

stages.title: Rebrand the product
stages.summary: Change identity, metadata and support details as one system.

tasks.title: Map brand locations
tasks.description: Identify product name, logo, palette, domain, support, email, metadata and legal touchpoints before editing.

tasks.title: Review the rebrand
tasks.description: Verify public pages, builder, account areas, emails, metadata, icons and social previews use the approved identity.

stages.title: Configure templates
stages.summary: Select and test layouts for the chosen audience.

tasks.title: Choose the template scope
tasks.description: Decide which existing templates to keep, adapt or hide before adding new designs.

tasks.title: Test content and PDF behaviour
tasks.description: Verify switching, long content, page breaks, photos, typography, preview and PDF output.

stages.title: Configure backend and auth
stages.summary: Prepare data, access, admin and recovery controls.

tasks.title: Review access and admin controls
tasks.description: Fix privilege boundaries, validate RLS and keep service-role credentials server-side before production use.

tasks.title: Define the data lifecycle
tasks.description: Document guest sync, consent, retention, deletion, backups, recovery and incident ownership.

stages.title: Configure AI or career features
stages.summary: Include only tools with clear value, privacy and cost controls.
stages.condition: Complete only for tools included in the launch scope

tasks.title: Define each tool state
tasks.description: Mark each tool live, retained but disabled, future, or excluded and keep the interface copy consistent.

tasks.title: Add provider safeguards
tasks.description: For provider-backed tools, document data sent, credentials, quotas, rate limits, failure behaviour and a non-AI path.

stages.title: Define the free and premium boundary
stages.summary: Decide what remains useful for free before enabling payment work.

tasks.title: Write the premium value proposition
tasks.description: State which optional value is paid and why the free product remains useful.

tasks.title: List payment completion work
tasks.description: Cover webhook verification, entitlements, idempotency, refunds, failures, reconciliation and support before activation.

stages.title: Prepare SEO and content
stages.summary: Create an initial original content cluster around real intent.

tasks.title: Choose the first content cluster
tasks.description: Select a small set of related role, audience or country intents the product can serve well.

tasks.title: Create original useful pages
tasks.description: Include reviewed examples, specific guidance, clear intent match and a relevant builder action without doorway duplication.

stages.title: Test production flows
stages.summary: Verify critical user, privacy and recovery paths before launch.

tasks.title: Test the user journey
tasks.description: Verify guest and account builders, persistence, templates, scoring, preview, PDF, mobile, errors and accessibility.

tasks.title: Test operating safeguards
tasks.description: Verify access controls, admin security, deletion, backups, recovery, monitoring and support escalation.

stages.title: Launch
stages.summary: Release a bounded product with clear ownership and monitoring.

tasks.title: Complete the launch decision
tasks.description: Confirm brand, domain, infrastructure, auth, email, privacy, support, content and production acceptance evidence.

tasks.title: Set launch monitoring
tasks.description: Assign owners for errors, support, usage signals, backups, recovery and rollback decisions.

stages.title: Acquire initial users
stages.summary: Test one permitted acquisition channel and learn from completion behaviour.

tasks.title: Run one bounded channel test
tasks.description: Choose a permitted SEO, community, referral, directory, partnership or content experiment for the selected audience.

tasks.title: Review user quality
tasks.description: Compare builder starts, meaningful progress, previews and downloads without inventing demand or conversion claims.

stages.title: Measure and improve
stages.summary: Use evidence to choose the next product improvement.

tasks.title: Review the product funnel
tasks.description: Measure defined visitor, builder, completion, preview, download, return and optional premium events with consent-aware analytics.

tasks.title: Choose one next improvement
tasks.description: Prioritise one evidenced friction point and define its acceptance and privacy requirements before implementation.
